abstract: Rice blast caused by Magnaporthe oryzae threatens rice production, and genomic prediction may accelerate identification of resistant germplasm. We evaluated classical machine-learning and simulated quantum-kernel models for binary and three-class prediction of leaf blast (BL) and panicle blast (PB) resistance in 204 rice accessions with 2,120 repeated phenotypic observations. Models used 328,597 single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs), 104,068 phased haplotypes, or 49,451 unphased haplotypes. Binary prediction outperformed three-class prediction. The highest binary macro-F1 scores were 0.87 for BL and 0.73 for PB. Phased and unphased haplotypes reduced predictor dimensionality by 68.3% and 85.0%, respectively, while retaining broadly comparable performance. Quantum support vector classification achieved competitive results in selected binary tasks but did not consistently exceed the strongest classical models. These findings establish a benchmark for SNP- and haplotype-based prediction of rice blast resistance and for evaluation of quantum machine learning in crop genomics.
